record.field: Website: controllers, QWeb, Bootstrap, SCSS, PDF
Build the adoption pages of the website: the animals waiting for a family, their page and the adoption form.

field.name: description
field.p: The animal shelter Les 4 Pattes takes care of 15 cats, dogs, rabbits and birds. Ten of them are waiting for a family, but nobody knows it: the shelter has no adoption page on its website yet.
Complete the module trivia_animal_shelter: the models, the backend and the data are ready, the website is up to you. The TODOs of the code are numbered like the tasks below.

ol.li: The adoptable animals (models/shelter_animal.py): the method _get_adoptable_animals(), the business logic of the pages.
The page /adopt (controllers/main.py, views/website_templates.xml): a public page with a responsive grid of cards, one card per adoptable animal.
The page of an animal: its URL is animal.website_url, e.g. /adopt/rex-6.

The adoption request (models/shelter_adoption_request.py and the same files): a form on the page of the animal, posted to the website, which creates the request safely with _create_from_website(). Then adopt an animal yourself, as a visitor, from a private window!
Style and menu (static/src/scss/shelter.scss, __manifest__.py): the SCSS file in the assets of the website, and an Adopt menu on the website.
The adoption certificate (report/adoption_certificate_report.xml): a PDF report printable from an adoption request.

field.p: ⭐ Bonus: buttons to filter the animals by species, and an Animal of the week building block for the website editor.

💡 Keep the controllers thin: the checker tests the methods of the models directly. After a change of Python code, or a new file or record, update the modules (make update). The website is at /adopt, open it in a private window to see it as a visitor.
